messages:
Maya: FYI got a ticket from Acme — they removed ~120 users from their Okta group yesterday but ~37 of them still show as active in Redwood.
Maya: Ticket link: https://support.redwood.ai/t/ACME-8432
Maya: Customer says SCIM responses for the PATCH succeeded (200) but users remain associated with the product role (editor) in UI and via API.
Diego: Can you paste the SCIM PATCH payload and the user IDs? curious if we see externalIds or if they used replace vs remove.
Maya: payload snippet from their logs:

```http
PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/00g7abcd1234
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>

{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    {"op": "remove", "path": "members[value eq \"00u1userA\"]"},
    {"op": "remove", "path": "members[value eq \"00u1userB\"]"}
  ]
}
```

Maya: Log shows 200 and group member count decreased on their side.
Sam: Any recent deploys to SCIM sync? I vaguely remember we flipped a cache layer for group->role lookups last week.
Diego: yep — we enabled the mapping cache (group_role_map) on 1794000000 to reduce DB hits. TTL 15m.
Diego: If a group is PATCHed and our webhook doesn't invalidate that cache key, the system can miss the removal until TTL expires or a manual recompute runs.
Maya: Customer says some of those users were re-added to different groups within minutes after the removal (bulk AD sync), might be a race.
Sam: Ok repro hypothesis: sequence is 1) group members removed in Okta -> Okta PATCH -> our webhook processes and updates Group table but fails to invalidate cache if externalId changed in same batch 2) AD bulk re-add -> another PATCH where externalId changed or group rename -> cache key mismatches -> leftover membership entries not reconciled.
Maya: They attached a sample GET we run against our SCIM API showing the users still present:

```http
GET /scim/v2/Users?filter=externalId eq "00u1userA"
200 OK
{
  "totalResults": 1,
  "Resources": [
    {"id": "u_1234", "userName": "alice@acme.com", "active": true, "roles": ["editor"], "groups": ["platform-team"]}
  ]
}
```

Diego: can you also pull the webhook delivery logs from ops-automation for that timeframe? looking for 2 things: receipt of PATCH and whether our delivery handler returned 202 vs 200, and any cache-invalidation errors.
Maya: attached: ops-automation logs show the webhook handler returned 200, and we queued an async job "scim:reconcile_group_membership" for group id=00g7abcd1234 but the job failed with a transient DB deadlock and then retried once.
ops-automation: job scim:reconcile_group_membership failed: PG::DeadlockDetected at 2026-03-12T18:23:11Z — retry scheduled
Sam: deadlock might have prevented the reconciliation step that removes memberships. If the job fails after we updated the group row but before we remove the user_role join rows, they remain.
Diego: this is a combined problem: (A) cache can't be relied on for immediate consistency during concurrent batches, (B) reconcile job isn't transactional with idempotent retry, (C) our webhook flow doesn't mark the job succeeded if the DB deadlock occurs after partial changes.
Maya: Customer is asking for root cause and fix — they're worried about stale access on terminated employees.
Sam: short term: run a targeted backfill for Acme group — run admin endpoint to force full reconciliation: `POST /admin/scim/reconcile?group_id=00g7abcd1234` (internal only).
Diego: I just kicked that off manually for the customer's org. ops-automation reported 37 orphaned membership deletions processed and 0 failures.
ops-automation: scim-sync-bot: Recon job started by Diego; deleted 37 stale user_role rows, flagged 0 failures.
Maya: sent confirmation to customer that we fixed their orphaned users and asked for a post-mortem of their sync timing — they responded :thumbsup:
Maya: For longer-term fix we should:
- invalidate group_role_map cache on any Group PATCH/PUT/DELETE and on member-level ops
- make reconcile job transactional and detect partial success to avoid silent deadlocks
- add a short-term metric/alert for "orphaned_members_detected" per org
Diego: Agreed. I'll open a PR to ensure cache invalidation on group webhook handler and add a small unit test for group rename + member changes.
Sam: I'll own making the reconcile job idempotent and adding a retry backoff + deadlock-specific handling. Plan to have a patch out in 48h.
Diego: created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/2789 (cache invalidation for SCIM group webhooks)
Sam: created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/2790 (reconcile job idempotency + deadlock handling)
Maya: assigning follow-ups — I'll email the customer with the remediation timeline and link both GH issues.
Maya: closing the ticket once they confirm in 24h, keeping this thread open for any follow-ups.
scim-sync-bot: scheduled background job scim:org_backfill (org=acme) to run nightly for 3 days to catch any remaining stale memberships.
Diego: tl;dr - root cause: cache TTL + transient reconcile job failure during a bulk sync race. Fixes underway and we've backfilled for this customer.
Sam: will post the postmortem once PRs are merged and we have metrics in prod.
Maya: thanks everyone. :heart:
